incentive_fee_mechanics.source: Note 3 Related Party Agreements and Transactions
incentive_fee_mechanics.base_management_fee: 1.75% per annum (0.4375%/quarter) of NAV as of the final business day of the PRIOR calendar quarter, capped so it cannot exceed 1.50% per annum (0.375%/quarter) of the lesser of (i) the average of gross assets (excluding cash/equivalents, including assets bought with borrowings) at the end of the two most recently completed quarters and (ii) the average monthly value of such gross assets during the most recently completed quarter. Payable quarterly in arrears. The fee base is NAV, so it falls automatically as marks fall — Q2'26 management fee 5,132 vs 6,079 in Q2'25.
incentive_fee_mechanics.income_incentive_fee_hurdle: Preferred return of 1.75% per QUARTER (7.00% annualized) of NAV at the beginning of each applicable quarter, computed over a Trailing Twelve Quarters look-back. A second gate applies: the incentive fee is payable only if pre-incentive fee NII in the CURRENT quarter also exceeds 1.75% x beginning-of-quarter NAV.
incentive_fee_mechanics.catch_up: 100% catch-up above the preferred return up to a catch-up amount equal to 2.1875% x NAV for each 'Legacy Fee Quarter' (quarters commencing before 2023-01-01) and 2.1212% x NAV for each 'Current Fee Quarter' (commencing on/after 2023-01-01).
incentive_fee_mechanics.incentive_rate: 20.00% for Legacy Fee Quarters and 17.50% for Current Fee Quarters of pre-incentive fee NII over the Trailing Twelve Quarters, subject to a per-quarter ceiling of 20.00%/17.50% of the CURRENT quarter's pre-incentive fee NII.
incentive_fee_mechanics.lookback_and_total_return_cap: YES on both. (a) Trailing Twelve Quarters look-back: the fee paid in a quarter is the excess of the cumulative computed fee over incentive fees on income already paid in the preceding eleven quarters. (b) Incentive Fee Cap (a total-return cap): 20.00%/17.50% of 'Cumulative Pre-Incentive Fee Net Return' over the trailing twelve quarters, where Cumulative Pre-Incentive Fee Net Return = pre-incentive fee NII over the trailing twelve quarters LESS any Net Capital Loss since April 1, 2018 (Net Capital Loss = aggregate capital losses, WHETHER REALIZED OR UNREALIZED, less aggregate capital gains, whether realized or unrealized), minus incentive fees on income paid in the preceding eleven quarters. If the Cap is zero or negative, NO incentive fee on income is payable.
incentive_fee_mechanics.cap_is_currently_binding: EFFECTIVELY YES. Incentive fees recognized were $0 for both Q2'26 and 1H26, versus 3,849 in Q2'25 and 10,282 in 1H25, and incentive fee payable was $0 at both 6/30/26 and 12/31/25. With 111,413 of net realized and unrealized losses in 1H26 alone feeding the Net Capital Loss term, the total-return cap is the operative constraint. This materially cushions reported NII against the mark deterioration — Q2'26 NII fell only 10.0% YoY while total investment income fell 16.0%, largely because the incentive fee went to zero.
incentive_fee_mechanics.capital_gains_incentive_fee: 17.50% of cumulative REALIZED capital gains, computed net of all realized capital losses AND cumulative unrealized capital depreciation, less previously paid capital gains incentive fees; determined and payable annually in arrears. GAAP requires accrual of a theoretical capital gains incentive fee assuming all unrealized gains/losses are realized: there was NO accrual for the three and six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025.
incentive_fee_mechanics.does_pik_count_toward_pre_incentive_fee_: NOT EXPLICITLY STATED IN THIS 10-Q — recorded as a coverage gap. The 10-Q does not reproduce the 'deferred interest feature / accrued income not yet received in cash' definitional language. However the filing's own risk-factor language states: 'in accordance with GAAP and tax regulations, we include in income certain amounts that we have not yet received in cash, such as contractual PIK... Since we may recognize income before or without receiving cash representing such income, we may not be able to meet the requirement to distribute at least 90%...'. Pre-incentive fee NII is a GAAP-NII-derived construct with no PIK carve-out disclosed, so PIK almost certainly counts; the definitive definition lives in the Investment Advisory Agreement / Form 10-K, not here.
incentive_fee_mechanics.merger_related_fee_adjustment: In connection with the Mergers, the Company and the Investment Adviser agreed that for incentive fee purposes, any amortization/accretion of purchase premium or discount to interest income, or gains/losses arising solely from ASC 805 cost-basis accounting adjustments on AFT/AIF assets, are EXCLUDED.

adviser_relationship_and_waivers.investment_adviser: Apollo Investment Management, L.P. ('AIM'), an affiliate of Apollo Global Management, Inc. ('AGM'). Administrator is Apollo Investment Administration, LLC ('AIA'). Maryland corporation incorporated 2004-02-02, externally managed BDC and RIC.
adviser_relationship_and_waivers.midcap_financial_relationship_as_disclos: The ONLY MidCap Financial Services, LLC arrangements disclosed in this 10-Q are CLO sub-servicing: (a) Sub-Servicing Agreement dated 2023-11-02 for MFIC Bethesda CLO 1 LLC at $145/year, accruing from 2025-10-23 — $45 paid in Q2'26 and $70 in 1H26 ($0 in both 2025 periods); (b) CLO2 Sub-Servicing Agreement dated 2025-02-24 for MFIC Bethesda CLO 2 LLC at $100/year — $25 paid in Q2'26 and $50 in 1H26 ($0 in both 2025 periods). The 10-Q does NOT quantify MidCap-Financial-originated or MidCap-sourced assets and does not describe a MidCap Financial origination/referral arrangement.
adviser_relationship_and_waivers.co_investment: SEC exemptive order received 2025-05-14 permitting co-investment with other AIM/affiliate funds. Co-investment holdings were 88% of the portfolio at fair value ($2,439,075) and 85% at cost ($2,610,570) at 6/30/26, vs 87% ($2,754,947) and 85% ($2,856,364) at 12/31/25. The Adviser Allocation Policy explicitly permits AIM to decide an investment 'is not appropriate for us', in which case it is not allocated to MFIC.
adviser_relationship_and_waivers.fee_waivers_and_reimbursements: Q2'26 / 1H26 expense reimbursements of 62 / 124 vs 280 / 1,086 in Q2'25 / 1H25 (income statement line). Note 3 attributes the 2026 amounts to the Merx Administration Agreement (administrative service expense reimbursements of $62 and $124 for Q2'26 and 1H26, vs $249 and $1,017 in the 2025 periods); debt expense reimbursements were $0 in both 2026 periods vs $30 and $69 in 2025. Financial Highlights footnote (4) refers to 'voluntary fee waivers' for the six months ended June 30, 2025 but only to 'expense reimbursements' for 2026 — the voluntary waiver appears to have LAPSED. Without them the 1H26 annualized total expense ratio would be 12.34% vs 12.32% reported (1H25: 13.10% vs 12.94%).
adviser_relationship_and_waivers.merx_related_party_arrangements: Merx, a wholly-owned portfolio company, has an administration agreement with AIA for an annual fee of $250 effective 2026-01-01. The 2019 Fee Offset Agreement (which credited MFIC 20%, stepping to 10%, of AIM aviation management/incentive fee revenue against incentive fees payable) was TERMINATED effective 2023-02-21 along with the Research Support and Technical Support Agreements, for a $7.5 million termination fee. Merx continues to service certain legacy Apollo aircraft investments under an Amended Servicing Agreement during its wind-down.

aft_aif_merger.detail: Merger Agreements signed 2023-11-07 with Apollo Senior Floating Rate Fund Inc. ('AFT') and Apollo Tactical Income Fund Inc. ('AIF'), each via a two-step merger sub structure. MFIC stockholders approved 2024-05-28; AFT/AIF stockholders approved at reconvened meetings 2024-06-21; acquisitions COMPLETED 2024-07-22.
aft_aif_merger.accounting: Asset acquisition method under ASC 805-50 (purchase accounting); assets recognized at cost to the acquirer including transaction costs, with no gain or loss unless the fair value of non-cash consideration differs from carrying amounts. Because the fair value of net assets acquired EXCEEDED the merger consideration paid, MFIC recognized a DEEMED CONTRIBUTION FROM THE INVESTMENT ADVISER — part of the acquired NAV arrived as an adviser-funded credit rather than as earned return.
aft_aif_merger.mark_integrity_relevance: The ASC 805 cost-basis reset means amortized cost for the AFT/AIF-acquired book is a 2024 purchase-accounting basis, not original underwriting basis, so FV/cost on those assets is not comparable to organically originated positions. The adviser separately agreed to strip ASC-805-driven premium/discount amortization and cost-basis gains/losses out of the incentive fee calculation, which is an explicit acknowledgment that the reset distorts reported income.
aft_aif_merger.capital_raised: Through 6/30/26 MFIC has raised approximately $2,680,207 in net proceeds from offerings including the AFT and AIF Mergers, and has repurchased common stock for $375,000.
